examples.ko: 그는 성적이 좋다고 교만해지면 안 돼요.
examples.en: He shouldn't get arrogant just because his grades are good.
If you speak in an arrogant way, people dislike it.

examples.ko: 처음 만났을 때는 좀 교만해 보였어요.
examples.en: When we first met, he seemed a bit arrogant.
Don't act arrogantly; behave humbly.
The boss isn't arrogant and is kind to the staff.
The more arrogant a person is, the less they admit mistakes.

explain: 반대말은 '겸손하다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '건방지다', '잘난 척하다', '거만하다'를 더 자주 말하고, '교만하다'는 조금 무겁고 글 같은 느낌이에요. 어떤 사람의 성격이나 태도를 평가할 때 써요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '겸손하다' (humble). In everyday talk people more often say '건방지다', '잘난 척하다' or '거만하다', while '교만하다' feels a bit heavy and written. It is used to judge a person's character or attitude.

examples.ko: 긴말할 필요 없이 결과로 보여 드릴게요.
examples.en: No need to say much; I'll show you with results.
I don't have time today, so I won't go on at length.
He didn't say much and just nodded.
Talking at length won't change anything.
I don't want to drag it out, so I'll start with the conclusion.

examples.ko: 긴말하면 오히려 변명처럼 들릴 것 같아요.
examples.en: If I go on at length, it might sound like an excuse.

explain: 대부분 '긴말하지 않다', '긴말할 필요 없다'처럼 부정이나 거절하는 말투로 나와요. 명사 '긴말'을 써서 '긴말 안 할게요', '긴말 필요 없어요'라고도 해요. 결론만 말하겠다고 할 때 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in negative or dismissive forms like '긴말하지 않다' or '긴말할 필요 없다'. People also use the noun '긴말', as in '긴말 안 할게요'. It is natural when you say you'll just give the conclusion.

examples.ko: 복잡한 신청 방법을 단순화해야 사람들이 쉽게 써요.
examples.en: If you simplify the complicated application method, people can use it easily.

examples.ko: 설명을 너무 단순화하면 틀린 내용이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you oversimplify the explanation, it can become inaccurate.
The designer simplified the app screen.

examples.ko: 규칙을 단순화하면서 예외는 몇 개만 남겼어요.
examples.en: While simplifying the rules, they kept only a few exceptions.
If you simplify the problem in your mind, it's easy to solve.

examples.ko: 일을 단순화하지 말고 하나씩 꼼꼼히 확인하세요.
examples.en: Don't oversimplify the work; check each item carefully.

explain: 보통 '을/를' 앞에 규칙, 절차, 설명, 디자인 같은 것이 와요. '너무 단순화하다'는 중요한 부분을 놓친다는 안 좋은 느낌이 있어요. 피동은 '단순화되다'예요.
explain_en: The object ('을/를') is usually something like rules, procedures, explanations or designs. 'Too much 단순화하다' carries a negative sense of missing important parts. The passive form is '단순화되다'.

examples.en: I pinned the paper to the bulletin board with a thumbtack.
It's dangerous to step on a tack that fell on the floor.
Please lend me a few thumbtacks.
I fixed the corners of the poster with thumbtacks.

examples.ko: 압정이 너무 짧아서 벽에 안 박혀요.
examples.en: The tack is too short, so it won't go into the wall.

examples.ko: 압정 상자를 쏟아서 한참 줍고 있어요.
examples.en: I spilled the box of tacks and have been picking them up for a while.

explain: 게시판이나 벽에 종이를 고정할 때 눌러 꽂는 작은 핀이에요. '압정을 꽂다', '압정을 박다', '압정으로 고정하다'처럼 써요. 끝이 뾰족해서 바닥에 떨어지면 위험하니까 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: It is a small pin you press in to fix paper to a bulletin board or wall. Typical patterns are '압정을 꽂다', '압정을 박다' and '압정으로 고정하다'. The point is sharp, so be careful when one falls on the floor.

examples.en: This work is also an extension of the last project.

examples.ko: 그 말은 어제 싸움의 연장선에서 나온 거예요.
examples.en: That remark came as a continuation of yesterday's fight.
I opened a small shop as an extension of my hobby.
This book is a continuation of the previous one.
If you think of it as a continuation of study, it's not hard.

examples.ko: 선을 길게 그어서 연장선을 만들어 보세요.
examples.en: Draw the line longer to make an extension line.

explain: 연장선은 원래 선을 더 길게 이은 선인데, 일이나 생각이 앞의 것에서 이어진다는 뜻으로 많이 써요. '~의 연장선에서', '~의 연장선이다'로 자주 말해요. 완전히 새로운 시작을 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: 연장선 is literally a line extended further, but Koreans mostly use it to say that a task or idea continues from something before. It often appears as ~의 연장선에서 or ~의 연장선이다. It is not used for a completely fresh start.

examples.en: If you have any questions about the contract, please ask.
If you jot down your questions, it's easier to ask them.

examples.ko: 설명을 듣고도 몇 가지 의문점이 남았어요.
examples.en: A few questions remained even after the explanation.
I tried organizing the doubtful points in this report.
I looked for more material to settle my questions.

examples.ko: 아무도 그 사고의 의문점에 답하지 못했어요.
examples.en: No one could answer the open questions about the accident.

explain: '의문점이 있다·생기다·남다·풀리다'처럼 같이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '궁금한 점'이 훨씬 자연스럽고, '의문점'은 회의·보고서·뉴스처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 써요. '의심'은 믿지 못하는 마음이라 의문점과 달라요.
explain_en: It goes with verbs like '있다', '생기다', '남다', and '풀리다'. In everyday talk '궁금한 점' is much more natural; '의문점' fits meetings, reports, and news. '의심' means not trusting, which is different.

examples.en: Let's stop here for today and take a rest.
Sir, you can stop around here.

examples.ko: 이야기는 이쯤 해 두고 밥 먹어요.
examples.en: Let's leave the talk at that and eat.

examples.ko: 물이 이쯤 차면 불을 꺼 주세요.
examples.en: When the water fills up to about here, please turn off the heat.
I think this is enough of an explanation.
By this point, I start wanting to give up.

explain: 정도, 장소, 때를 모두 가리킬 수 있어서 '이쯤에서 그만하자', '이쯤 하면 충분해요'처럼 마무리할 때 자주 써요. 말하는 사람에게 가까우면 '이쯤', 듣는 사람 쪽이면 '그쯤', 멀면 '저쯤'을 써요. 비슷한 말로 '이 정도'가 있어요.
explain_en: It can refer to degree, place or time, and is often used to wrap things up, as in '이쯤에서 그만하자'. Use '이쯤' for what is near the speaker, '그쯤' for near the listener, and '저쯤' for far away. '이 정도' is a similar expression.

examples.en: This picture is my own creation.

examples.ko: 남의 창작물을 허락 없이 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not use someone else's work without permission.
Creative works have copyright.
That work is popular overseas too.
Do you want to go to the exhibition of creative works together?
Would a work made by AI also have copyright?

explain: '작품'은 예술적으로 완성된 것이고, '창작물'은 직접 새로 만들어 낸 것이라는 점이 강조돼요. 저작권이나 인터넷 콘텐츠 이야기에서 '창작물'이라는 말이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 작품 stresses a finished piece of art, while 창작물 stresses that someone made it from scratch. It comes up often when talking about copyright or online content.

examples.ko: 새 공항 후보지가 세 곳으로 정해졌어요.
examples.en: Three candidate sites were chosen for the new airport.
Our city was also listed as a candidate site for the Olympics.

examples.ko: 회사가 새 공장 후보지를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is looking for candidate sites for a new factory.

examples.ko: 이 섬은 영화 촬영 후보지로 거론돼요.
examples.en: This island is mentioned as a possible filming location.
I visited both candidate sites and compared them.
The candidate sites will be announced next week.

explain: '후보'는 사람과 물건에 두루 쓰지만 '후보지'는 어디에 지을지, 어디서 열지 아직 정해지기 전의 장소에만 써요. 뉴스에서 '건설 후보지', '개최 후보지'로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 후보 works for people and things, but 후보지 is only for places not yet decided on, such as where to build or hold something. You see 건설 후보지 and 개최 후보지 in the news.
